English: Reed Net Stand
Simple stands of reeds, lashed together and set along the shore to hang basic nets for drying and mending. Provides a focal point for the first fishers to gather.
Boat Shelter
A crude shelter of driftwood and reeds, protecting small fishing boats from the elements and encouraging a more organized settlement.
Fish Drying Rack
Rows of wooden racks for drying and preserving fish, allowing for safe storage and trade of the catch.
Canoe Slipway
A shallow ramp and flat area for launching and repairing canoes, speeding up fishing efforts and transportation.
Simple Wharf
A modest wooden wharf extends into the water, enabling easier unloading of catch and simple trade with passing vessels.
Fishermens Hut
Sturdy huts for the families of fishermen, with communal storage and shared hearths. Fosters a sense of unity and draws new settlers.
Fish Market
A bustling market for fresh and salted fish, attracting traders and increasing prosperity for the settlement.
Salt House
A stone warehouse for storing and producing salt, essential for preserving fish and supporting large-scale trade.
Seafood Pavilion
A grand pavilion where the finest catches are auctioned and festivals are held, drawing visitors and further strengthening the local economy.
Iberian Harbor
A fortified harbor with stone quays, cranes, and customs houses, serving as a hub for mercantile and naval power on the coast.
